\[
c_{j+1} = (h * c_j)\downarrow_2,\quad d_j = c_j - g * (c_{j+1}\uparrow_2),
\qquad
w_{j,k} = \operatorname{DFB}_k(d_j),
\qquad
T_{j,k} = \kappa\, \sigma\, s_{j,k},
\qquad
\hat{c}_j = \operatorname{DFB}^{-1}\big(\eta_{T_{j,\cdot}}(w_{j,\cdot})\big) + g * (\hat{c}_{j+1}\uparrow_2),
\qquad
J = 3,\ K = \text{8},\ \kappa = 3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(c_j\): The coarse image at level j, c_0 is the channel
- \(d_j\): The band at level j, the detail the coarser level cannot predict
- \(h, g\): The 9-7 analysis and synthesis low-pass filters, 9 and 7 taps
- \(w_{j,k}\): The coefficients of directional subband k of band j
- \(\sigma\): The noise level of the channel
- \(s_{j,k}\): The noise gain of subband k of band j
- \(\kappa\): The threshold factor
- \(\eta_T\): The shrink rule with threshold T

The image channel is c_0. The Laplacian pyramid of Burt and Adelson makes a coarse image c_j+1 with the low-pass filter h. It keeps the difference d_j to its prediction with the filter g. The filters h and g are the biorthogonal 9-7 filters. The directional filter bank, DFB, splits each band d_j into K subbands w_j,k, each holding edges in one wedge of directions. It is a tree of two-channel quincunx filter banks. Each bank is a ladder of two steps with the filter B, so it rebuilds exactly whatever B is. The noise level of the image is sigma. The noise gain s_j,k is the standard deviation that white noise of level 1 has in subband k of band j. The shrink rule eta is the one of wavelet thresholding. The coarse image c_J is kept. With kappa 0 every step is undone exactly.
